subject: middle children
one_liner: Priority delivery for the child listed under “and the others.”
brand_voice_notes: A confident retail operation selling measurable parental attention. Dry order statuses and procurement language. No therapeutic promises. Every benefit has a small administrative defect.

hero.h1:
Someone remembered.
We have the receipt.
hero.sub: Second is the marketplace for middle children. Order an unprompted phone call, a correctly named birthday cake, or a gift-parity audit. We track the acknowledgment from dispatch to dinner.

features.title: Attention, on subscription.
features.blurb: Schedule one unprompted question about your life every month. Our AI supplies the follow-up, so “work is fine” no longer closes the ticket.

features.title: Gift parity, independently audited.
features.blurb: Submit both gifts for a retail-value comparison, including batteries. Get a discrepancy notice and an equal-value gift recommendation. Sentimental value remains outside the return window.

features.title: Your name. On the cake.
features.blurb: Reserve a birthday acknowledgment with a two-hour delivery window. Spelling is checked against your account, rather than your older brother.

pricing_tiers.name: Also included
pricing_tiers.tagline: A foothold in the family account.

pricing_tiers.name: First this time
pricing_tiers.tagline: Priority handling for the usual fallback.

pricing_tiers.name: Only for billing
pricing_tiers.tagline: The economics of being an only child.

demo_screen_concept: A shopping screen for the Mercer family account. Search and filter four attention products, add quantities to an order, choose standard or priority handling, see live line totals and place a mock order with a receipt. An attention ledger shows 12 monthly units: 5 eldest, 3 middle, 4 youngest. A birthday cake starts in the basket at $24; gift-parity audit is $18, unprompted call $12, saved dinner seat $9. Gift-parity audit compares both gifts and supplies a discrepancy notice and equal-value gift recommendation. Call capacity is three slots, reduced live as calls enter the basket and restored on removal. Each basket and receipt line keeps its fulfillment date: cake on the birthday, 2–4 pm; call tomorrow, 2–4 pm; audit report tomorrow; seat at Sunday dinner. Priority processing adds $8 and processes the order immediately instead of within one hour; product delivery dates do not change.

design_direction.style: Parcel-catalog modernism: broad orange merchandising bands, ice-gray stockroom surfaces, heavy compact sans headings and offset tab edges. Crisp retail layout with asymmetric full-bleed campaign art.
design_direction.archetype: Marketplace / Directory from bundled library. Merchandising hero, campaign artwork, service catalog benefits, allocation explainer, customer evidence and subscription plans. Demo uses search, department filters and an order basket.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 160ms color feedback on buttons; user-triggered basket count and receipt updates. No ambient animation. Reduced motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: An ice-gray nav with the accepted petrol logo, expansive orange headline field with low aligned CTA, then a full-width campaign composition inside a quiet ice-gray margin. Feature benefits appear as open horizontal product specifications, not repeated cards. Wide allocation artwork beside live-text explanation. Three subscription columns on white. Demo is a practical white shopping floor with a petrol order sidebar.
design_direction.design_review: Read latest seven concepts and their recorded motifs. No tuple matches. Rejected automatic pixel-game typography and generic blue/green palette because this is an adult retail bureaucracy. E-commerce Clean pairing is from bundled library. Identity is folded parcel-tab merchandising, distinct from lightstick tickets, film programmes, sports timing and noticeboards. Boldness concentrated in orange headline and campaign artwork.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: Amazon-style ordering and fulfillment are recast as procurement of family attention. A middle parcel tab physically projecting ahead of its neighbors makes birth order into a shipping priority. No Amazon smile or source trademark; no mascot. It differs from recent entries through folded-paper retail graphics and a mechanical custom wordmark.

logo.concept: Accepted Gemini direction A: three folded parcel tabs, central petrol tab projects above and below its neighbors with orange fold planes. Bespoke Second wordmark includes an e-c crossbar junction. B rejected as a generic ribbon.
logo.clear_space: At least half the symbol height on all sides, included in exports
logo.placement: Landing navigation and footer; demo chrome; cropped symbol favicon on both pages

images.rationale: Five successful calls: two logo directions, one composed campaign and two infographic attempts. Accepted A gets deterministic mono/icon exports. No photo slots needed. Related art used the accepted logo as an actual reference. First infographic corrected once for repeated stack labels.

items.prompt: Design a finished original brand identity artwork for Second, a premium deadpan online marketplace that lets middle children order parental attention as if it were a shipment. Exact wordmark text: "Second". No other text. NOT a presentation board, no mockups, no multiple variants in one image. Horizontal lockup, a custom symbol on the LEFT and bespoke wordmark on the RIGHT, ample clean margin. Palette deep petrol #12343B and saturated orange #EE5A24 on uniform ice gray #EDF2F3. Do not copy Amazon, no smile or swoosh. Concept direction A: three folded parcel-label tabs with the central one pulled forward and upward. Give the symbol a distinctive folded silhouette readable at 24px, and give the lettering restrained mechanical charm with one considered custom junction. Sophisticated retail logistics, not children's clip art. Flat graphic design, no shadows, no gradients, no texture. Make mark and wordmark one coherent design, use most horizontal space, no fine lines.
items.verdict: A accepted: exact Second spelling and deliberate e-c junction. Strong center-tab silhouette at nav size and 32px icon. B ribbon less specific. Crop keeps half-symbol-height exterior space in page brand link.

items.transformation: Threshold foreground of accepted source and map both inks to solid petrol; same crop and contour
items.verdict: Same accepted silhouette; folded facets merge in one ink as expected.

items.transformation: Isolate accepted left symbol from original source, preserve margins, resize to 128x128
items.placement: Local favicon on both pages and product order receipt
items.verdict: Three-tab silhouette and orange folded facets remain visible at 32px.

items.prompt: Create a professionally composed retail campaign artwork for Second, the marketplace for middle children to order parental attention. Attached image is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE, not an edit target: preserve its exact symbol, letterforms and petrol/orange relationship wherever you show the logo. Landscape 3:2 poster. A bold cut-paper sculptural illustration of THREE shipping parcels on a low shelf, with the middle parcel dramatically pulled forward, larger and orange; the two side parcels in quiet petrol and ice gray. Integrate a folded dispatch label and an illustrated cake silhouette on the central parcel, not a UI screenshot. Strong asymmetric Swiss retail advertising composition, giant typography and generous negative space, fine paper tooth, flat shapes with considered folded planes. Exact intentional text only: "For once, yours first." as the large headline; "Attention. Packed to order." as smaller supporting line; approved Second logo small at bottom. All spelling exact, no extra text, no watermark. Palette #EE5A24, #12343B, #EDF2F3, #F7CF5F. Keep text away from edges, readable when image is 360px wide. This is a designed illustrated campaign, not a photograph, no generic geometric background or diagram.
items.verdict: Accepted: exact headline and supporting line, three parcels with orange middle leading, cake receipt illustration, approved tab logo retained. Composed paper sculpture and type, not a captioned photo. At 360px headline and supporting copy read; small artwork logo supplemented by navigation logo.

items.prompt: Targeted correction to attached infographic. Reference 1 is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE (Second logo); reference 2 is the EDIT TARGET infographic. Preserve the beautiful folded-paper three-stack composition, palette, hierarchy and type personality. Correct the repeated labels: remove ALL text from the individual parcel units. There must be exactly FIVE plain unlettered parcel units in left stack, THREE plain unlettered orange parcel units in middle stack, FOUR plain unlettered parcel units in right stack. The 12 units must be visibly separate and countable. Put ONE large label BELOW EACH COMPLETE STACK on the background: "Eldest 5" below left; "Middle 3" below center; "Youngest 4" below right. These three labels each appear exactly ONCE. Top headline exactly "12 units. One family." Bottom small sentence exactly "Same family. Different handling." Approved Second logo at lower right without changing its letterforms. No other text, no watermark, no numbers on parcels. Landscape 3:2. Leave generous background around each label and keep mobile legibility. This is a composed editorial infographic with cut-paper shipping sculpture, not a basic bar chart.
items.placement: Landing allocation section with live-text summary
items.verdict: Accepted corrected composition: countable five eldest, three middle and four youngest parcel units, one label per stack. Uppercase headline is intentional artwork typography with correct wording. Logo and folded-paper medium match campaign. Fine paper planes remain distinguishable at 360px; live HTML repeats every quantity.

discarded.prompt: Create one finished original logo lockup for "Second", a marketplace where middle children procure family attention. Only exact text "Second". A distinct direction B: a bold continuous folded packing-ribbon symbol forming a center notch, beside bespoke wide lowercase-inspired lettering that still spells "Second" with capital S. The middle is brought to the front. Horizontal symbol-left / wordmark-right composition. Flat deep petrol #12343B and orange #EE5A24 on uniform #EDF2F3. No Amazon smile, no source trademark, no rounded-square badge, no mascot, no gradients, no mockup, no board. Large open counters, deliberate kerning, broad clear margins. Finished small-size retail identity, graphic quality over ornament.
discarded.verdict: Rejected after comparison: ribbon resembles a generic interlocked badge; less direct birth-order hierarchy than A. Raw removed.

discarded.prompt: Design a complete high-quality illustrated infographic for Second using the attached approved logo as the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE. Preserve its exact symbol and wordmark if included. This is a family attention allocation data story, NOT a screenshot or simple flowchart. Landscape 3:2 composition in cut-paper retail catalog graphic design, flat shapes with folded planes and slight paper tooth. Exact headline: "12 units. One family." Three substantial shipping-label stacks or receipt ribbons form an imaginative but precise visual comparison: Eldest has FIVE units, Middle has THREE, Youngest has FOUR; total 12. Make each unit visibly countable and identical in height, dark petrol eldest, orange middle, muted petrol youngest, on #EDF2F3 ground with yellow #F7CF5F accents. Strong typographic hierarchy. Exact labels: "Eldest 5", "Middle 3", "Youngest 4". Small footer exact text: "Same family. Different handling." Small faithful Second logo optional. All labels large enough to read at mobile width; no small print, no extra copy, no watermark, no gradients, no photographs. Compose illustration, type and numbers together as intentional editorial information design. No simple HTML-style bars or arrows.
discarded.verdict: First composition has correct countable 5/3/4 stacks but repeats the total label on each parcel. Request one targeted correction to label each complete stack once. Raw removed.
